name: Tunisia
snapshot: The birthplace of the Arab Spring has slid back into one-man rule under Kais Saied, who dissolved parliament in 2021 and jailed many of his critics.
culture: Tunisia was home to Carthage, and its Roman ruins, the holy city of Kairouan and the whitewashed village of Sidi Bou Said draw visitors. Its personal status code of 1956 gave women more rights than anywhere else in the Arab world. Malouf music, inherited from Andalusia, and a lively cinema and theatre scene thrive. Couscous and harissa are central to the table.
society: Tunisia's 2011 revolution toppled Zine El Abidine Ben Ali and began the Arab Spring. Economic stagnation, high youth unemployment and shortages of basic goods have followed. Sfax is a key departure point for migrants to Italy, and Saied's remarks about sub-Saharan migrants in 2023 set off attacks against them.
situation: Kais Saied, a law professor elected in 2019, suspended parliament in 2021 and rewrote the constitution to give himself sweeping power. He won a second term in October 2024 with 91 percent after rivals were jailed or disqualified. In 2026 the courts went further: in February an appeals court upheld and increased prison terms for opposition leaders and former security officials in the mass conspiracy case, and in September the top court confirmed the convictions.
power: A presidential republic under the 2022 constitution, which concentrates power in the president, who appoints and dismisses the government and can rule by decree. Parliament is weak and the judiciary has been brought under presidential control.
